operational_pain.finding: The whole package business runs through a phone line and nothing else. Packages are the highest-value bundle they sell, cruise plus one of their own two hotels plus rail or motorcoach, and there is no online path to buy one.
operational_pain.verbatim_quote: Packages are available to book by phone only unless noted in the package description. Discounts are valid on new reservations only. All discounts must be booked directly with Major Marine Tours, and are not valid through third-party reservations or travel agencies.

operational_pain.finding: That phone line is open 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., seven days, year-round. Their first cruise of the day departs at 8:00 a.m. and their published check-in rule puts guests on the dock at 7:00 a.m., a full hour before anyone can answer a phone. Their last cruise returns at 7:00 p.m., an hour after the line closes.
operational_pain.verbatim_quote: Customer Service Hours: 8:00 a.m. - 6:00 p.m. 7 days a week
operational_pain.confidence: fact for the hours and the departure times, INFERENCE for the gap

operational_pain.finding: Their own published check-in rule is impossible to obey for a major inbound flow. They require check-in one hour before departure, and they simultaneously sell the 11:30 am cruise as the connection off a train that arrives at 11:15 am. Guests arriving by rail have fifteen minutes, not sixty.
operational_pain.verbatim_quote: Please check in one hour prior to your cruise departure time for all cruises*
operational_pain.confidence: fact for both statements. The train timing is on the same site: 'The train arrives in Seward at 11:15 a.m. and the cruise departs at 11:30 a.m.' https://majormarine.com/faq/

operational_pain.finding: The contingency for a late train is manual, discretionary and unpromised. Every late arrival becomes a human judgment call about moving a party to another date or downgrading them to a shorter, cheaper cruise, which means a partial refund calculation too.
operational_pain.verbatim_quote: If the train arrives late, we will do our best to transfer passengers to a different date or to the 4 Hour Cruise that departs at 12:30pm.

operational_pain.finding: The refund and reschedule policy has four different clocks running at once, plus a per-person fee and a card fee. A front-line agent has to know which clock applies to which booking before quoting anything.
operational_pain.verbatim_quote: Cruise-only reservations are refundable up to 72 hours prior to your cruise departure. A 3% credit card processing fee will be retained for cancellations. [...] $15 per person re-booking fee [...] completely non-refundable and may not be used on any other sailings.
operational_pain.confidence: fact. Other clocks on the same page: hotel packages refundable 'until 7 days prior to the first day of your package reservation, within 7 days the package is non-refundable and non-changeable', and packages including 'motorcoach or train' are 'refundable until 21 days prior'. One free date change is allowed if made within 24 hours of departure, and the $15 per person fee applies to changes after that.

operational_pain.finding: Weather re-routes are a routine, captain-initiated event that produces a case-by-case partial refund on the cruise while the bundled hotel and transport stay non-refundable. Every one of those is a manual money decision and a manual customer conversation, and the exposure sits on the busiest days.
operational_pain.verbatim_quote: Our cruises go out rain or shine. We only cancel cruises due to unsafe sea conditions, in which case we will notify you as soon as possible.
operational_pain.confidence: fact. The refund side is on the policy page: cruises may be 'limited to the confines of Resurrection Bay', in which case partial refunds apply, while additional services 'remain non-refundable and non-changeable'. Decision authority sits with the Coast Guard-certified Captain.

operational_pain.finding: The complimentary Seward shuttle, which covers a long list of pickup points, can only be added by telephone with 24 hours notice, and it is excluded from the earliest cruise of the day.
operational_pain.verbatim_quote: Please call us to add the shuttle to your reservation at least 24 hours before your cruise for your convenience. [...] Advance reservations are required for shuttle pick-up. [...] Shuttle is not available for the 8:00 am 6 Hour Kenai Fjords National Park Cruise.

operational_pain.finding: Cruise ship day-callers have to be moved 0.6 to 0.8 miles from the terminal inside a 165-minute window, on a 15-minute headway, and that window closes before the 10:00 am departure.
operational_pain.verbatim_quote: A complimentary Major Marine Tours shuttle will make continuous loops between Harbor 360 Hotel, the South Harbor office, and the Cruise Ship Terminal from 7:00 am. - 9:45 a.m., departing every 15 minutes.

operational_pain.finding: Every seat is manually assigned by staff before sailing, and special seating is explicitly not guaranteed. With eight vessels and up to seven departure slots a day at peak, that is a large recurring manual allocation job.
operational_pain.verbatim_quote: Seating arrangements are assigned by Major Marine Tours staff prior to the cruise. Special seating requests can be made, but we cannot guarantee requests until all seating arrangements are made.

operational_pain.finding: Dietary and accessibility requests are captured at the point of reservation and vary by vessel, so a booking change can silently break an accommodation. Wheelchair access differs vessel by vessel and three named boats have none.
operational_pain.verbatim_quote: Vegetarian guests on the 6 Hour Cruise, 7.5 Hour Cruise and 8.5 Hour Cruise can request a vegetarian sandwich in advance, at the time of reservation.
operational_pain.confidence: fact. Same page on access: accessible on the first deck inside cabin only for Glacier Express, Skana, Spirit of Adventure, Spirit of Matushka and Kenai Fjords 360, while 'The Viewfinder, Orca Song (8.5-hour cruise), and Rachel Marie (12:30pm 4-hour departure) are not wheelchair accessible' and 'None of our vessels can accommodate motorized wheelchairs.'

operational_pain.finding: They rebuild a large share of their Seward workforce from scratch every year, inside a three-month hiring window, and subsidise it with dorm beds and a completion-contingent travel payment.
operational_pain.verbatim_quote: During our cruise season we employ about 60 seasonal employees in Seward. Our peak hiring time for seasonal positions is January 15th - April 15th.

industry.industry: Small and mid-sized day-cruise, tour and activity operators. Seasonal, fixed-capacity, weather-dependent, mixed direct/OTA/wholesale/cruise-line distribution.
industry.headline: In this industry the measured wins are clustered at the two ends, and the middle, which is what gets sold hardest, is where the evidence is thinnest.

categories.category: 1. Reservations, booking and rebooking, self-serve change and cancellation

whats_working.claim: AI-assisted self-service now resolves over 40% of customer issues end to end with no human agent, up from roughly one third the prior quarter, and support cost per booking fell about 10% year over year.
Expedia handles more than 250 million service interactions a year, over half resolved through self-service, and more than 30% of those self-service resolutions are AI-powered.
whats_working.who: Ariane Gorin, CEO Expedia Group, Q1 2026 earnings call

whats_working.claim: Website chatbots wired into the reservation system produced attributed booking revenue at three named boat/activity operators in 2025, including a small New England day-cruise operator.
whats_working.who: TOMIS; named customers Cap'n Fish's Cruises, Body Glove Hawaii, Nashville Pedal Tavern
whats_working.measured_outcome: Cap'n Fish's: 2,977 messages, $106,113 attributed revenue, 9.6% bot conversion. Body Glove Hawaii: 1,635 messages, $874,244 attributed revenue. Nashville Pedal Tavern: 660 messages/month, $86,058.

whats_working.claim: Airbnb's production stack for cancellation/refund handling is NOT one big model: it is narrow intent-detection classifiers plus a refund-ratio predictor trained on historical human agent decisions, feeding a self-resolve flow. Q&A-style binary intent classification outperformed multi-class intent classification both offline and online.

whats_not_working.claim: AI chat is not yet a booking channel. LLM referrals are under 1% of room nights at the largest OTA in the world, with 'no material change over the last few months or quarters'.
whats_not_working.who: Ewout Steenbergen CFO and Glenn Fogel CEO, Booking Holdings Q2 2026

whats_not_working.claim: AI referral traffic to independent hotel sites is roughly 1% of total visits and about 3.1 to 3.2% of organic search traffic.
whats_not_working.who: Lighthouse website analytics via eHotelier (dataset size not disclosed, a real limitation)

whats_not_working.claim: The headline AI feature from the largest tours-and-activities reservation platform has shipped no named customer and no number. 'Currently rolling out to a select group of operators.'
Abandoned-booking recovery, widely marketed as AI, is a fixed timing rule in at least one major platform: abandoned after 1 hour of inactivity, recovery email 8 hours later. No model, no prediction.

categories.solid_ground: Answering pre-booking questions with LIVE availability wired in, and closing the sale inside the conversation. Every case with a real number has the same ingredient: the assistant is connected to the reservation system, not just to a FAQ document. The self-serve refund/change decision is also solid, but ONLY where the decision has been decomposed into narrow classifiers over historical human decisions (Airbnb's pattern), not handed to a general chatbot.
categories.soft_ground: AI as an acquisition channel. Under 1% of room nights at Booking Holdings and ~1% of visits at independent hotels. Anyone selling 'get booked by ChatGPT' as this season's revenue is selling a 2028 thesis at 2026 prices.
categories.what_would_have_to_be_true: The booking system must expose live availability to an assistant. Named tour-operator cases run 233 to 3,000 conversations per month, so a compressed-season operator should measure its own peak-week inquiry volume before assuming it clears that bar. Watch attribution: '$874,244 attributed revenue' is chat-touched revenue, not proven incremental revenue, and NO vendor in this space publishes a holdout test.

categories.category: 2. Inbound phone handling and after-hours coverage, voice agents

whats_working.claim: Independent, externally-measured end-to-end voice latency across five major platforms lands between 1,296ms and 1,740ms median, with p95 tails from 1,768ms to 2,259ms.
whats_working.who: Openbenchmarks. A caller robot dials the agent over a real phone call, both sides recorded on one clock, Silero VAD for turn boundaries, measured from call audio rather than platform self-reporting. 432 calls and 2,078 usable turns per platform.
whats_working.measured_outcome: Telnyx 1,296ms median / 1,856ms p95. ElevenLabs 1,424 / 1,768. Bland AI 1,520 / 2,248. Vapi 1,558 / 2,008. Retell AI 1,740 / 2,259.

whats_working.claim: Across 12 live production voice deployments, containment ran 62 to 88% with a fleet median of 78%, at $0.07 to $0.21 all-in per minute.
whats_working.who: DestiLabs, own client telemetry. Explicitly NOT third-party validated, customers not named.

whats_not_working.claim: NO named tour or activity operator has published a containment rate, a call-abandon rate, or a latency figure for its own voice agent. The measured voice numbers all come from horizontal vendors and benchmarks, not from this industry.
whats_not_working.who: Absence finding across Yonder, FareHarbor, Peek, Ventrata, TOMIS, Myma, Arival, PhocusWire and four voice benchmark sources

whats_not_working.claim: Real production voice systems are three to four times slower than the marketing number. Not one of five platforms achieved sub-800ms median in external measurement; all five exceeded 1,200ms.

categories.solid_ground: Narrow, high-frequency, after-hours intents with a booking link as the exit: departure times, what to wear, where to park, is the 2pm sailing full, send me the link. Containment in the 60-88% band on that scope is consistent across every source found. Economics are genuinely small now, single-digit cents per minute.
categories.soft_ground: Anything that has to be right the first time on a live sailing day, and anything conversational and open-ended. At 1,300-1,700ms per turn a caller feels the pause, and glacier-cruise callers are often calling BECAUSE something has gone sideways, which is the worst moment to make them wait. Voice is the single most agent-washed category in this vendor field.
categories.what_would_have_to_be_true: Somebody has to count the calls first. Needs to know how many calls arrive outside staffed hours, what fraction are the same six questions, and what a missed call is worth when a seat is perishable within hours. Needs a clean transfer path to a human during operating hours, and a hard rule that the bot never touches a same-day cancellation or a safety question.

categories.category: 3. Weather-driven cancellation, re-accommodation and proactive guest messaging

whats_working.claim: The closest thing to a measured win is decomposed refund/cancellation decisioning: predict the refund ratio from historical human agent decisions, classify who initiated and whether both sides agree, then let the parties self-resolve.
Bulk weather-cancellation tooling with automated rebooking credits and manifest-wide cancel already exists inside the mainstream tour platforms, as DETERMINISTIC RULES rather than AI.

whats_not_working.claim: THIS IS THE THINNEST POCKET IN THE WHOLE INDUSTRY. Across every search run, no named tour, cruise or activity operator has published a measured outcome from AI applied to weather cancellation, re-accommodation or proactive disruption messaging. Everything found was vendor marketing describing the capability in the future tense.
whats_not_working.who: Absence finding after four distinct search angles

categories.solid_ground: The mechanics: threshold rules (wind, wave height, ceiling), bulk notify, reschedule-first credit rather than refund, and logging WHY each cancellation happened and how it resolved. This is deterministic software, testable exhaustively, most of it already sitting unused inside the reservation platform, and per the feasibility ladder it should be built before any model is considered.
categories.soft_ground: AI-authored empathy at the moment of cancellation, and agentic auto-re-accommodation. Nobody in this industry has published a number for it. A tone-deaf message to a family who flew to Alaska for one glacier day is an expensive error with an unforgiving cost profile, exactly the shape where the scoping doctrine says either do not use AI or wrap it in human review.
categories.what_would_have_to_be_true: Cancellation reasons and resolutions would have to be captured as structured data FIRST. Most operators this size record them in a note field or not at all, so a model has nothing to learn from. The AI-shaped part is narrow: drafting the message for a human to approve, and classifying inbound refund requests into policy buckets. The re-accommodation decision itself is a rules problem with a fixed manifest and a known set of remaining departures.

categories.category: 4. Seasonal hiring, onboarding, training a crew that turns over every year, and knowledge capture

whats_working.claim: THE STRONGEST INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE IN THIS REPORT. A generative AI assistant raised customer-support productivity 14% on average, and 34% for novice and low-skilled workers, with minimal effect on experts, by disseminating the practices of the most able workers to newcomers.
whats_working.who: Erik Brynjolfsson, Danielle Li, Lindsey R. Raymond, NBER Working Paper 31161, field data from 5,179 customer support agents
whats_working.measured_outcome: +14% issues resolved per hour overall; +34% for novices; minimal for experienced staff; also improved customer satisfaction and employee retention; mechanism identified as knowledge diffusion from high performers down the experience curve

whats_working.claim: A day-cruise operator found the guest-facing chatbot became a staff training tool as a side effect, because new crew used it to look up the same answers guests were asking for.
whats_working.who: Paul Milligan, Chief Executive, Black Cat Cruises (Akaroa NZ, ~100-pax vessel, 4-5 daily departures)
whats_working.measured_outcome: Qualitative, described as an unexpected staff training tool benefit. Same deployment: 500 conversations/month, 10 staff hours saved/month, 60% of questions answered, 15 clickthroughs/month, ~$3,750/month in referred bookings.

whats_not_working.claim: No named tour or cruise operator has published a measured onboarding-time or ramp-time reduction from an AI knowledge tool. The measured evidence in this category is horizontal, not industry-specific.

categories.solid_ground: THE MOST UNDER-SOLD AND BEST-EVIDENCED POCKET FOR AN OPERATOR OF THIS EXACT SHAPE. The Brynjolfsson finding is tier 1, large-n, and its mechanism is precisely the problem a seasonal operator has: a workforce that is permanently novice because it resets every May, and expertise that walks off the dock every September. The corpus also already exists and is bounded, which is the rare case where retrieval is honestly scoped: crew manuals, safety briefings, the narration script, the wildlife and glacier interpretive material, the answers to the twenty questions every guest asks, and the tribal knowledge about which berth, which tide, which bus connection.
categories.soft_ground: Retrieval over a messy, growing, unpermissioned pile. Precision degrades as the corpus grows, and confident wrong answers about a safety procedure are a serious cost of error. Also soft: AI in hiring and screening, where no measured evidence was found in this industry and the legal exposure is real.
categories.what_would_have_to_be_true: Someone has to own the corpus. Bounded, current, deduplicated, with citations back to the source document so a 22-year-old deckhand in week two can check the answer. There must be an eval set of real questions from real crew before it goes live, and an honest 'I do not know' path. The knowledge-capture half, interviewing departing staff into structured notes at end of season, is a September project, not an April one, and it is the piece nobody sells because it is not a product.

categories.category: 5. Demand forecasting, dynamic pricing, yield and capacity management

whats_working.claim: Dynamic and variable pricing is now standard capability in the tours/attractions reservation platforms, and half of all operators are using or testing AI tools of some kind.
whats_working.who: Arival Global Operator Landscape 4th Edition, 5,664 qualified survey responses collected Aug-Nov 2025 across six languages, reported secondhand because Arival's own pages return 403
whats_working.measured_outcome: 50% of operators actively using or testing AI, up from about one third in 2024; enterprise operators 68%; OTA share of bookings 37% (up from 33%), direct website 25% (down from 29%)

whats_not_working.claim: The one AI dynamic-pricing product built for this industry publishes a revenue range with no named customer, no method and no denominator: claimed 5-15% additional revenue, 18% revenue recovery from abandoned bookings, 33% waitlist conversion.
whats_not_working.who: Peek Pro, Peek AI Dynamic Pricing

categories.solid_ground: Shoulder-season demand volatility is the real and widely-shared pain, 42% of operators name it as their top challenge. Rules-based tiered and time-of-day pricing is proven, deterministic and already sitting in the platforms. Forecasting FOR STAFFING is a more tractable target than forecasting for price, because the cost of being wrong is smaller and the feedback loop is daily.
categories.soft_ground: ML-driven yield management at this scale. A two-port operator with a roughly 120-day season and a handful of daily departures generates on the order of a few hundred to low thousands of departure-days per year, and most of the variance is driven by three exogenous things a model cannot see: the cruise ship berthing schedule, the weather, and the wholesale contract. Thin data with dominant exogenous drivers is the classic setup for a model that looks great in backtest and does nothing in production.
categories.what_would_have_to_be_true: Three or more seasons of departure-level booking-curve data (bookings by days-out, by channel, by fare class, not just totals), willingness to test price elasticity on a subset of departures, and a channel structure that permits price variation. If a meaningful share of seats are pre-committed to cruise-line shore-excursion desks and wholesalers at contracted rates, the addressable inventory may be too small to be worth the model. Answer that BEFORE building.

categories.category: 6. Reviews, guest communications and multilingual guest handling

whats_working.claim: Operators themselves report the highest positive impact from AI in content and analysis, NOT in guest-facing bots.
whats_working.who: GetYourGuide proprietary research, n=505 travel experience operators, surveyed March 2026, published alongside Arival's Global Operator Landscape 4th Ed. Vendor-run but sample, date and partner disclosed.
whats_working.measured_outcome: 84% product descriptions, 81% web/blog, 78% business planning and analysis, 74% SEO content. 64% use AI more than a year ago. 56% say AI tools feel overwhelming. 44% report receiving inaccurate or misleading information from AI tools.

whats_working.claim: Multilingual guest handling at high straight-through rates is real and deployed at named travel companies.
whats_working.who: Freeday.ai; named customers CitizenM (36 properties) and Prijsvrij
whats_working.measured_outcome: CitizenM 93% straight-through processing. Prijsvrij 225,000 interactions handled with no headcount increase.

whats_not_working.claim: RESPONDING TO REVIEWS HAS ESSENTIALLY ZERO EFFECT ON WHETHER AN LLM RECOMMENDS YOU. In a 61,459-call algorithm audit across 12 models, management response moved recommendation probability by +0.1 percentage points, statistically indistinguishable from zero, while guest rating moved it +31.6pp and review volume +8.3pp. The paper notes explicitly that management response is 'a cue the optimization industry actively promotes'.
whats_not_working.who: Baig, Gillani, Ali; randomized choice-based conjoint audit, 3,024 choice sets per model across 12 models, 3 personas, 9 prompt templates, position randomized
whats_not_working.measured_outcome: Guest rating 4.7 vs 3.9 stars +31.6pp; price $249 vs $129 -30.0pp; eco-certification +11.6pp; review volume 2,100 vs 45 +8.3pp; recency +1.6pp; chain affiliation -1.8pp; management response +0.1pp. First-position listing advantage worth about $11.7/night.

whats_not_working.claim: The vendor's own headline chatbot answer rate is materially higher than the number in its own named-customer case study: 95% claimed vs 60% measured at Black Cat Cruises.

categories.solid_ground: Two things. First, generating review VOLUME and protecting the RATING, because those are the two signals that measurably move both human bookers and machine recommenders (+8.3pp and +31.6pp). Second, drafting: descriptions, listing copy, itinerary text, FAQ, translated versions. That is where 505 real operators say they are getting value, low cost of error because a human reads it before it ships, and it needs no integration at all.
categories.soft_ground: AI review RESPONSES sold as visibility optimisation. Respond for the human reader and for Google if you like, but the tier 1 audit says it does not move LLM recommendation. Also soft: any 'get recommended by AI' package priced against a channel currently ~1% of traffic.
categories.what_would_have_to_be_true: For review generation: a reliable post-trip contact capture, which is the hard part for an operator whose seats arrive via OTAs, wholesalers and cruise-line shore-excursion desks that do not always pass the guest's email through. THAT DISTRIBUTION GAP, NOT THE AI, IS THE CONSTRAINT.

categories.category: 7. Back office: refunds and policy exceptions, channel reconciliation, payroll and scheduling

whats_working.claim: Automated transaction coding and account reconciliation saved a named multi-location hospitality operator up to 25 hours a month and closed the month 5 to 10 days faster.
whats_working.measured_outcome: Up to 25 hours/month saved; month-end close accelerated 5-10 days. Comparators: Quora invoice processing from 5-8 minutes to 1-2 minutes per invoice.

whats_working.claim: Channel commission leakage is a real, quantified, under-policed loss, and the mechanism is exactly the one a small operator would recognise: nobody checks the invoice line by line, so a tolerance band hides the leak.
whats_working.who: Sean Anderson, CRO, RobosizeME, in Hospitality Net. Customer described as a 400-property European hotel group but NOT named.
whats_working.measured_outcome: Up to $40,000 a month overpaid in OTA commissions, because short-staffed teams only checked whether invoices fell within a plus or minus 1% tolerance band

whats_working.claim: One of the four major tour reservation platforms publicly DECLINES to ship generative AI and instead tells operators to fix their booking data first, describing itself as 'the operational backbone that 99% of operators need before they can even consider AI'.

whats_not_working.claim: No named tour or activity operator has published a measured reconciliation, refund-processing or payroll outcome from AI. The measured back-office numbers all come from adjacent industries.
AI staff scheduling savings figures (around 15% labour cost, around 25% overtime reduction) trace to hotel-industry marketing content, not to a named operator or an independent study.

categories.solid_ground: Reading messy documents and matching them against a known record. That is the one node in the back office where AI genuinely earns its place on the feasibility ladder, because the input is unstructured (a wholesaler's PDF remittance, an OTA commission statement in a different format each month, a shore-excursion desk manifest) and the check itself is deterministic. Everything downstream of extraction, the matching, the flagging, the ledger write, should be plain code. The Ramp/Adrift shape, 25 hours a month, is the realistic order of magnitude for a business of this size, not a transformation.
categories.soft_ground: Autonomous refund and policy-exception decisions. Airbnb only got there by training a refund-ratio model on years of logged human agent decisions; a 60-person operator does not have that dataset and probably does not log the decision at all. Also soft: AI payroll and scheduling, where the seasonal multi-vessel tide-and-ship-schedule constraint structure is a SOLVER problem, not a learning problem.
categories.what_would_have_to_be_true: You would need to actually be losing money to the channel gap for this to pay, and that is a countable question: pull three months of wholesale and OTA remittances and reconcile them by hand once. If the variance is near zero, the project is dead and you saved the money. If it is not, you now have the baseline and the eval set in the same afternoon. THE CHEAPEST TEST IN THE WHOLE REPORT AND IT NEEDS NO AI TO RUN.

where_its_working_vs_where_they_expect.what_operators_expect_to_buy: A guest-facing AI, usually a chatbot or a voice agent, sold on 24/7 coverage and 'get found by ChatGPT'.
what_the_evidence_actually_supports: END ONE, CONTENT AND KNOWLEDGE. The largest sample of real operators in this industry (n=505, March 2026) reports its highest positive impact in the least glamorous places: product descriptions 84%, web and blog content 81%, business planning and analysis 78%, SEO content 74%. No integration, low cost of error, human reads it before it ships. Alongside that sits the strongest independent finding in the whole report, +34% productivity for novice workers via knowledge diffusion from experienced staff (Brynjolfsson/Li/Raymond, n=5,179), which maps onto a crew that resets every May better than it maps onto almost any other business in America.

END TWO, DOCUMENT-HEAVY BACK OFFICE. Reading a wholesaler's remittance or an OTA commission statement and matching it to your own record. Named-customer evidence exists (Adrift Hospitality, 25 hours/month) and the failure mode it catches is quantified elsewhere (up to $40,000/month of unchecked commission leakage at a 400-property group).

THE MIDDLE, GUEST-FACING BOTS, IS REAL BUT SMALLER THAN THE PITCH. It works when wired to live availability, and there are named day-cruise operators with numbers: Black Cat Cruises, 500 conversations and 10 staff hours saved per month, 60% of questions answered, about $3,750/month in referred bookings. Quicksilver Cruises, 233 conversations and 10.3 hours saved per month. True, useful, modest numbers from businesses shaped like this one. Not 12x ROI, and the same vendor publishes both.

THE THING THEY ARE MOST LIKELY TO BE MIS-SOLD RIGHT NOW is AI-search visibility. Two independent measurements say the channel is not there yet, and the specific lever most often sold for it, responding to reviews, moved LLM recommendation probability by +0.1 percentage points in a 61,459-call audit. Statistically zero.
where_its_working_vs_where_they_expect.the_one_sentence_that_saves_money: If a vendor is selling this operator a guest-facing AI on the promise of AI-search visibility and review-response optimisation, both halves of that promise are contradicted by tier 1 measurement, while the two places with the best evidence, seasonal crew knowledge and channel reconciliation, are things nobody is calling them about.

hype_flags.claim: '12x ROI in the first 60 days' from an AI voice agent
hype_flags.why_its_hype: Yonder's own pages attribute this to TWO DIFFERENT customers. The voice-agent page credits Luthers Pontoon; the whitewater-rafting customer page credits Quarry Park Adventures. No investment base, no revenue base, no method, no time-boxed comparison. A vendor number that cannot keep its own customer straight cannot be repeated as fact.

hype_flags.claim: 'Our AI chatbot answers approximately 95% of guest questions'
hype_flags.why_its_hype: The same vendor's own named-customer case study reports 60% at Black Cat Cruises, a day-cruise operator of roughly the relevant shape. The 95% is a marketing ceiling, the 60% is what one real boat operator got. PLAN AGAINST THE 60%.

hype_flags.claim: AI dynamic pricing delivers '5-15% additional revenue'; abandoned-booking automation recovers 18%; waitlist conversion 33%
hype_flags.why_its_hype: Three performance ranges on one page, none attached to a named customer, none with a stated method, denominator or control. Exactly the 'vendor average used as this company's baseline' pattern the scoping doctrine bans.

A real number from a named operator, but 'attributed' is doing enormous work. No attribution window, no attribution model, no holdout. A guest who chatted then booked is counted; whether they would have booked anyway is not tested. Read every figure in this category as chat-touched revenue, not incremental. NO vendor in this space was found publishing a holdout or A/B result.

hype_flags.claim: 'AI is a booking channel now, get found in ChatGPT'
hype_flags.why_its_hype: Booking Holdings' CFO put LLM referrals under 1% of total room nights in Q2 2026 with no material change over several quarters, and Lighthouse measures AI referral traffic at just under 1% of independent hotel website visits. Visibility is rising, transactions are not.

hype_flags.claim: 'Responding to reviews improves how AI recommends you'
hype_flags.why_its_hype: A 61,459-call, 12-model audit measured management response at +0.1 percentage points, statistically zero. The authors specifically call it 'a cue the optimization industry actively promotes'.

Externally measured from real call audio across five leading platforms, medians ran 1,296ms to 1,740ms and p95 tails 1,768ms to 2,259ms. Vendor-instrumented figures are measured inside the platform and exclude parts of the path the caller actually experiences. When a vendor quotes latency, ask whether it was measured from the audio or from their own logs.

hype_flags.claim: 'AI cuts repetitive guest inquiries by up to 70%'
hype_flags.why_its_hype: Myma.ai publishes this with no named customer, no baseline and no measurement window. 'Up to' is a ceiling, not an expectation.
Published by an OTA that benefits from suppliers chasing review counts. Correlational milestone across listings of wildly different quality, age and price, presented as a causal threshold.

vendor_landscape_summary.FareHarbor: FareHarbor Agent announced 2026-04-27, 'rolling out to a select group of operators'. NO named customer, NO metric, NO price. Pricing model is no monthly subscription but a 6-8% booking fee added at checkout paid by the customer, plus ~2.9% + $0.30 card processing borne by the operator. CAVEAT: that pricing breakdown was fetched from CaptainBook, a direct FareHarbor competitor, so treat the framing as adversarial and verify on a call.
vendor_landscape_summary.Peek Pro: Peek AI Dynamic Pricing plus an n8n automation suite. Claims 5-15% additional revenue, 18% abandoned-booking recovery, 33% waitlist conversion, ALL unattributed.
vendor_landscape_summary.Ventrata + Satisfi Labs: Agentic ticketing agent launched 2026-07-14. Named customers One World Observatory (2.5x weekly in-chat revenue growth over 8 weeks, 3.1% click-to-confirmed-sale) and City Sightseeing New Orleans (1,800+ ticket interactions). Skews to high-volume hop-on-hop-off and major attractions, a larger profile than a 60-person operator.
vendor_landscape_summary.Checkfront: NO native gen AI, by public choice. Recommends a 90-day data-hygiene plan first. The notable signal in a field this noisy.
vendor_landscape_summary.Xola: Abandoned Reservation Recovery is a deterministic timing rule, not a model.
vendor_landscape_summary.Rezdy: No AI features on the fetched features page as of 2026-08-10.
vendor_landscape_summary.Yonder: Purpose-built third-party AI layer for tour operators. Chatbot, voice agent, review generation. Integrates with 13+ reservation systems. PUBLISHES PRICING, which is rare: chatbot $95/mo for 80 chats to $295/mo for 500; reviews and SMS from $75/mo. Month to month, explicitly supports downgrading during low season, which matters for a four-month operator. Named day-cruise customers Black Cat Cruises and Quicksilver Cruises.
vendor_landscape_summary.TOMIS: AI chatbot integrated to the reservation system with revenue attribution. Named customers Cap'n Fish's Cruises, Body Glove Hawaii, Nashville Pedal Tavern.
vendor_landscape_summary.Ramp: Horizontal back office. Named hospitality customer Adrift Hospitality, 25 hours/month.

base_rate_context.realistic_magnitude: For a business of this size the honest order of magnitude from the named-customer evidence is 10 to 11 staff hours saved per month on guest inquiries (Black Cat 10, Quicksilver 10.3), 60% of guest questions answered rather than 95%, a few thousand dollars a month of chat-referred booking value at a small day-cruise operator, and around 25 hours a month in the back office. EVERY headline in this industry an order of magnitude above those figures came from a vendor with no named customer attached.
base_rate_context.adoption: 50% of tours-and-activities operators are using or testing AI, up from about one third in 2024. 64% use AI more than a year ago, but 56% say AI tools feel overwhelming and 44% report having received inaccurate or misleading information from them. OTA share of bookings rose to 37% from 33% while direct website share fell to 25% from 29%.

thin_spots: ALASKA. NO published AI deployment by any Alaska tour, cruise or activity operator was found. Searched Major Marine Tours, Allen Marine, Kenai Fjords, plus Alaska SBDC, ATIA and Alaska trade press. This is an absence of published evidence, not evidence of absence. It also means there is no local reference customer to point at, and the prospect would be EARLY rather than late.
WEATHER CANCELLATION AND RE-ACCOMMODATION. The weakest category in the report. Four separate search angles found no named tour or cruise operator with a measured AI outcome.
VOICE, INDUSTRY-SPECIFIC. Solid independent latency and containment benchmarks exist, but ZERO named tour or activity operators have published their own containment, abandon or handoff numbers.
DYNAMIC PRICING AT SMALL SCALE. Plenty of platform capability, no named small or mid-sized fixed-capacity operator with a measured yield gain.

CRUISE-LINE SHORE-EXCURSION DESK CHANNEL. Searched specifically. Found cruise-line-side guest personalisation and booking marketing only. Nothing on the supplier-side operational seam, which for a two-port Alaska operator is likely one of the highest-friction parts of the whole business. GENUINELY UNMAPPED.

PAYWALLED AND BLOCKED SOURCES. Arival's research pages, PhocusWire and ScienceDirect all return 403 to automated fetching. Arival findings here are secondhand via Travel Professional News and GetYourGuide's published version.
industry.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH on categories 1, 2, 6 and 7, where multiple independent measurements and several named-customer cases from structurally similar day-cruise operators converge on the same modest, consistent magnitudes. MEDIUM on category 4, where the productivity evidence is tier 1, large-n and mechanistically on point but horizontal rather than tour-specific. LOW-MEDIUM on category 5. LOW on category 3, the report's genuine hole. Also LOW on Alaska-specific and on the cruise-line shore-excursion supplier seam, both of which appear to be unpublished rather than untried.
